text: [CONTEXT: Article I > Section 9] The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus shall not be suspended, unless when in Cases of Rebellion or Invasion the public Safety may require it. Because the clause sits in Article I, the suspension power is generally understood to belong to Congress.

subtopic: Appointments Clause & Officers of the United States
text: [CONTEXT: Article II > Appointments Clause] Any appointee exercising significant authority pursuant to the laws of the United States is an Officer of the United States and must be appointed by the President with Senate consent, or, if an inferior officer, by the President alone, the Courts of Law, or the Heads of Departments as Congress provides.

[CONTEXT: 14th Amendment > Equal Protection] Under strict scrutiny, government action classifying by suspect categories like race or national origin must be narrowly tailored to serve a compelling governmental interest.

[CONTEXT: 10th Amendment > Reserved Powers] Public health regulations, quarantines, and general safety measures fall within the states' reserved police power. Under the anti-commandeering doctrine, the federal government cannot compel state officers to administer or enforce a federal regulatory program.
